data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
#FLUX -J jacobiMPI
#FLUX -N 1
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=20
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=1
#FLUX --exclusive 
#FLUX --time=00:10:00

# NOTE: The original script's logic to check if running on a cluster ('if command -v sinfo')
# has been adapted. Flux does not have a single command equivalent to 'sinfo',
# so we check for the existence of the FLUX_JOB_ID environment variable instead.
# This variable is only set when running inside a Flux job.
if [ -n "$FLUX_JOB_ID" ]; then # if on cluster
    module load mpi/openmpi-x86_64
    # The 'pmi/pmix' module is likely not needed, as Flux's MPI integration
    # handles this automatically. It is kept for compatibility.
    module load pmi/pmix-x86_64
    mpiproc=20
else  # if on local machine
    mpiproc=4
fi

# 'mpirun' is replaced by 'flux run'. Flux will use the resource allocations
# defined by the job directives.
flux run -n $mpiproc ./jacobiMPI 128 1000
"
}
